public_rationale: The Guardian report published March 11, 2025 documents substantial difficulties across several Pac-Man attempts [e1, e2]. Justin Martin reported missing pellets, broken warp tunnels and frustrating debugging, then switched to Tetris after an hour [e1]. Hester reported generating an approximation in seconds, but it needed corrections and still lacked features including power pills and more levels [e2]. Another attempt received one star, with the reviewer questioning its colours, maze, ghosts and Pac-Man [e1]. Martin also called the process “surprisingly easy,” and other participants expressed enthusiasm [e2]. These accounts support the limited claim that the attempts involved substantial difficulties, alongside some quick progress and positive reactions [e1, e2].
limitations: The report does not establish universal failure or a population failure rate [e1, e2].
It does not establish that all seven participants lacked coding knowledge: Hester described software development experience, and Martin had studied programming in high school [e2].
March 11, 2025 is the publication date; the evidence does not establish when each coding session occurred [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In The Guardian's test, people using AI tools without coding knowledge did not succeed well at building a Pac-Man clone.

statement.excerpt: I don’t want spoil all the fun, but … things didn’t go well:

our_interpretation: Read the statement as a limited description of substantial difficulties in the reported attempts, not as a claim that every attempt failed completely.
Assess the findings of the particular Guardian report as published on March 11, 2025; this does not date every participant's coding session.
The separate characterization of the participants as seven people without coding knowledge is not assumed to be established by this outcome.
criteria.support_condition: The original account documents substantial implementation or debugging difficulties in the attempts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The original account describes consistently straightforward production of satisfactory, functioning clones.
